list_storage_accounts.title: List storage accounts in the subscription
list_storage_accounts.description: Every storage account in the subscription, with its SKU, kind, access tier, primary endpoints and network rules. The `primaryEndpoints` on each account are exactly the hosts the data-plane connectors need, so this is the call that tells you what to point `azure-blob-storage` and friends at.

output.description: Every storage account in the subscription.

items.description: id, name, location, sku, kind and properties (primaryEndpoints, accessTier, provisioningState, networkAcls, allowBlobPublicAccess, minimumTlsVersion).

list_storage_accounts_in_group.title: List storage accounts in a resource group
list_storage_accounts_in_group.description: The storage accounts in one resource group, with the same detail as list_storage_accounts. Cheaper when the group is already known.

resource_group.description: The resource group to look in.

output.description: The storage accounts in the group.

items.description: id, name, location, sku, kind and properties.

get_storage_account.title: Get a storage account
get_storage_account.description:
One account in full: SKU and replication, kind, access tier, encryption settings, network ACLs, whether public blob access and shared-key authorisation are allowed, minimum TLS version, and the primary and secondary endpoints.
This is the security posture of the account in one object -- `allowBlobPublicAccess`, `allowSharedKeyAccess`, `minimumTlsVersion` and `networkAcls.defaultAction` are the four fields an audit cares about.

expand.description: Extra properties to include, e.g. geoReplicationStats or blobRestoreStatus.

sku.description: Standard_LRS, Standard_GRS, Premium_LRS and so on.

properties.description: primaryEndpoints, accessTier, encryption, networkAcls, allowBlobPublicAccess, allowSharedKeyAccess, minimumTlsVersion and provisioningState.

create_or_update_storage_account.title: Create or update a storage account
create_or_update_storage_account.description:
Create a storage account, or change the settings of one that exists. The name must be globally unique across all of Azure and is 3-24 lowercase letters and digits -- check it with check_storage_account_name_availability first, because a taken name fails late and confusingly.
`sku` fixes the replication (LRS, ZRS, GRS, RAGRS) and `kind` the account type; StandardV2 with StandardV2... in practice, `StorageV2` with `Standard_LRS` is the general-purpose answer. Creation is asynchronous: poll get_storage_account for `provisioningState` Succeeded.
On an existing account this replaces the top-level fields you send, so send the security properties you want rather than assuming the current ones survive.
create_or_update_storage_account.notes: The account name is globally unique across Azure and cannot be changed afterwards.

resource_group.description: The resource group to create the account in.

account_name.description: The account name -- 3 to 24 lowercase letters and digits, globally unique.

sku_name.description: Replication and performance tier. Standard_LRS is local redundancy, Standard_ZRS zone redundancy, Standard_GRS geo-redundancy.

kind.description: Account kind. StorageV2 is the general-purpose one and what you almost always want.

access_tier.description: Default blob access tier for the account.

allow_blob_public_access.description: Whether containers may be made anonymously readable. Set false unless the account genuinely serves public content.

allow_shared_key_access.description: Whether the shared keys may be used at all. Setting false forces every caller onto Entra ID, and disables list_service_sas.

minimum_tls_version.description: Lowest TLS version the endpoints accept.

https_only.description: Reject plain HTTP on the data endpoints.

output.description: The account as created or updated.

update_storage_account.title: Patch a storage account's settings
update_storage_account.description:
Merge a change into an existing account -- tags, access tier, network rules, a security flag -- leaving everything else alone. Safer than create_or_update_storage_account for a small change, since a PUT resets what it does not carry.
Note that some fields cannot be changed after creation at all: the account's name, its region, and its kind.

tags.description: Tags to set on the account.

sku_name.description: Change the replication tier. Not every transition is allowed.

properties.description: Account properties to merge, e.g. {"allowBlobPublicAccess": false} or a networkAcls block. Anything omitted keeps its value.

delete_storage_account.title: Delete a storage account and all its data
delete_storage_account.description:
Destroy a storage account together with every blob, queue, table and file share inside it. Irreversible unless the account had point-in-time restore or account soft delete configured beforehand, which is not the default.
Call get_blob_service_properties first if you want to know whether any recovery is possible at all, and consider a management lock (`azure-resource-manager`'s create_management_lock) on accounts that should never be deletable.
delete_storage_account.notes: Destroys all data in the account. Recovery depends on soft delete having been enabled in advance.

check_storage_account_name_availability.title: Check whether a storage account name is free
check_storage_account_name_availability.description: Storage account names share one global namespace across all of Azure, so a name that looks obviously yours may well be taken by a stranger. This asks before you try, and the `reason` on a false answer distinguishes "AlreadyExists" from "AccountNameInvalid" -- which is worth knowing, because the rules are strict: 3 to 24 characters, lowercase letters and digits only.

output.description: Whether the name can be used, and why not if it cannot.

nameAvailable.description: True when the name is free.

list_account_keys.title: Get a storage account's shared keys
list_account_keys.description:
The account's two shared keys. Each one is unrestricted administrative access to every blob, queue, table and file share in the account, never expires, and cannot be scoped down -- so the response is a credential and must be handled as one, not logged or passed on.
Prefer list_service_sas or an Entra ID token wherever possible. There are two keys so that consumers can be moved to one while the other is rotated with regenerate_key; that is what they are for.
list_account_keys.notes: Returns live credentials granting full access to the account's data. Do not log the output.

expand.description: Set to kerb to include Kerberos keys for Azure Files identity-based access.

output.description: The account keys. Secret -- full access to all data in the account.

items.description: keyName (key1 or key2), value (the secret) and permissions (Full or Read).

regenerate_storage_account_key.title: Rotate one of a storage account's keys
regenerate_storage_account_key.description:
Replace one shared key with a new one. Everything still authenticating with the old value STOPS WORKING IMMEDIATELY -- applications, mounted file shares, and every SAS token that was signed with that key, which is the only way to revoke a SAS early.
The safe rotation is: move consumers to key2, regenerate key1, move consumers back to key1, regenerate key2. Rotating both at once is an outage.
regenerate_storage_account_key.notes: Immediately invalidates the old key and every SAS token signed with it.

output.description: Both keys, with the rotated one holding its new value.

list_account_sas.title: Mint an account-level SAS token
list_account_sas.description:
Create a shared access signature scoped to services, resource types and permissions across the whole account, valid until a fixed expiry. The right thing to hand to something that needs broad but time-limited access -- far better than passing a shared key, which never expires.
`services` is a string of letters: b blob, q queue, t table, f file. `resource_types`: s service, c container, o object. `permissions`: r read, w write, d delete, l list, a add, c create, u update, p process.
The token is signed with a shared key, so regenerating that key revokes it. There is no other way to revoke one early -- keep expiries short.
list_account_sas.notes: Returns a live credential. The only way to revoke it early is regenerate_storage_account_key.

services.description: Services the token covers -- any of b (blob), q (queue), t (table), f (file), concatenated.

resource_types.description: Resource types -- any of s (service), c (container), o (object), concatenated.

permissions.description: Permissions -- any of r, w, d, l, a, c, u, p, concatenated. Grant the least that works.

expiry.description: When the token stops working, ISO 8601 UTC. Keep it short.

start.description: When the token starts working, ISO 8601 UTC. Defaults to now.

ip_range.description: Restrict the token to a single IP or a range, e.g. "203.0.113.5-203.0.113.9".

accountSasToken.description: The query-string token to append to a data-plane url.

list_service_sas.title: Mint a SAS token for one container or blob
list_service_sas.description:
Create a shared access signature scoped to a single container, blob, queue or file share rather than the whole account -- narrower and therefore safer than list_account_sas.
`canonicalized_resource` is the full resource path including the account name, as in `/blob/prodsa/mycontainer`, and `resource` says whether that path is a container (c) or a blob (b).
Signed with a shared key, so regenerate_storage_account_key is the only early revocation. Keep expiries short.
list_service_sas.notes: Returns a live credential scoped to one resource.

canonicalized_resource.description: The resource path, including the service and account, e.g. "/blob/prodsa/mycontainer".

resource.description: b for a blob, c for a container, f for a file, s for a file share.

permissions.description: Permissions -- any of r, w, d, l, a, c, u, p, concatenated.

expiry.description: When the token stops working, ISO 8601 UTC.

start.description: When the token starts working, ISO 8601 UTC.

ip_range.description: Restrict the token to an IP or range.

stored_policy_id.description: Name of a stored access policy on the container to inherit permissions and expiry from. A SAS bound to one CAN be revoked by deleting the policy, unlike a free-standing one.

serviceSasToken.description: The query-string token to append to the resource url.

get_blob_service_properties.title: Get an account's blob service settings
get_blob_service_properties.description:
The account-wide blob settings: soft delete for blobs and containers and their retention days, versioning, change feed, point-in-time restore policy, CORS rules and the default service version.
This is where you find out whether a deleted blob is actually recoverable. Soft delete is off unless someone enabled it, and nothing on the data plane will tell you that.

properties.description: deleteRetentionPolicy, containerDeleteRetentionPolicy, isVersioningEnabled, changeFeed, restorePolicy and cors.

set_blob_soft_delete.title: Turn on blob soft delete
set_blob_soft_delete.description:
Enable (or disable) soft delete for blobs on the account and set how many days a deleted blob stays recoverable. Worth doing on any account holding anything that matters -- without it, a delete on the data plane is immediate and final.
Soft delete only protects blobs deleted AFTER it is enabled. Retention is 1 to 365 days.
set_blob_soft_delete.notes: Retention is billed -- soft-deleted blobs occupy storage until the window expires.

retention_days.description: How many days a deleted blob stays recoverable.

enabled.description: Whether soft delete is on. Setting false stops protecting future deletes.

output.description: The blob service configuration after the change.

list_containers.title: List an account's blob containers
list_containers.description:
The account's containers through the management plane, each with its public access level, lease state, immutability policy and legal hold. This is the governance view -- for listing what is *inside* a container, use the `azure-blob-storage` connector's own list_blobs.
`publicAccess` other than None means the container is readable by anyone on the internet, which is usually the finding an audit is looking for.

filter.description: Only containers whose name starts with this prefix.

include.description: Set to deleted to include soft-deleted containers.

items.description: id, name and properties (publicAccess, lastModifiedTime, leaseState, hasImmutabilityPolicy, hasLegalHold, deleted).

create_container.title: Create a blob container
create_container.description:
Create a container in the account. `public_access` decides whether it is anonymously readable: None (the default, and the right answer) keeps it private, Blob allows anonymous reads of individual blobs, and Container additionally allows anonymous listing -- which is how storage accounts end up indexed by search engines.
Public access also has to be allowed at account level (`allowBlobPublicAccess`) for anything but None to take effect.
create_container.notes: public_access of Blob or Container makes the contents readable by anyone on the internet.

container_name.description: The container name -- lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

public_access.description: None keeps the container private. Blob and Container expose it anonymously.

delete_container.title: Delete a blob container
delete_container.description: Destroy a container and every blob in it. Recoverable only if container soft delete was enabled on the account beforehand -- check get_blob_service_properties' `containerDeleteRetentionPolicy` first. A container with a legal hold or an active immutability policy cannot be deleted at all.

container_name.description: The container to destroy, with everything in it.

list_file_shares.title: List an account's file shares
list_file_shares.description: The Azure Files shares on the account, with their quota, used capacity, access tier and protocol (SMB or NFS). The quota is a hard limit -- a share that is full rejects writes -- so this is the call to make when Azure Files starts refusing them.

expand.description: Set to stats to include each share's used capacity.

items.description: id, name and properties (shareQuota, accessTier, enabledProtocols, shareUsageBytes when expanded).

create_file_share.title: Create a file share
create_file_share.description:
Create an Azure Files share on the account. `quota_gb` is a hard cap, not a billing hint: on a standard account the share is billed for what it uses, but writes fail once the quota is reached, so size it with room.
SMB is the general-purpose protocol; NFS requires a premium FileStorage account.

share_name.description: The share name -- lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

quota_gb.description: Maximum size in GiB. Writes fail once the share reaches it.

protocol.description: SMB works on any account; NFS needs a premium FileStorage account.

access_tier.description: Storage tier for the share, on standard accounts.

delete_file_share.title: Delete a file share
delete_file_share.description: Destroy a file share and everything in it. Recoverable only if share soft delete is enabled on the file service; otherwise final. Anything currently mounting the share loses it immediately.

get_lifecycle_policy.title: Get the account's blob lifecycle policy
get_lifecycle_policy.description: The rules that automatically tier or delete blobs by age -- the mechanism behind blobs quietly moving to Cool or disappearing after N days. When data has gone missing and nobody deleted it, this is usually the answer.

output.description: The lifecycle management policy, or 404 when none is set.

properties.description: policy.rules, each with a filter and the tier-to-cool, tier-to-archive and delete actions.

set_lifecycle_policy.title: Set the account's blob lifecycle policy
set_lifecycle_policy.description:
Replace the account's lifecycle rules wholesale -- this is a PUT, so the rules you send become the entire policy and any existing rule not re-sent stops applying. Read get_lifecycle_policy first.
A rule with a `delete` action deletes blobs automatically and permanently (subject to soft delete). Get the `daysAfterModificationGreaterThan` thresholds wrong and data disappears on a schedule, so this is worth treating as a destructive change even though the call itself only writes configuration.
set_lifecycle_policy.notes: A full replace of the policy, and a delete rule removes data automatically from then on.

rules.description: The complete rule set, each entry {"enabled": true, "name": "...", "type": "Lifecycle", "definition": {"filters": ..., "actions": ...}}. Replaces the existing policy entirely.

properties.description: The stored policy and its lastModifiedTime.

get_storage_usage.title: Get storage account quota usage in a region
get_storage_usage.description: How many storage accounts the subscription has in a region against the limit it is allowed. The answer to a create that failed with a quota error, and worth checking before a bulk provisioning run.

output.description: Storage account usage against quota in the region.
